step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard shows an architecture for an internal developer platform at OLX Autos. Key components visually drawn include: User (external actor), Route 53, ALB, EKS, Spot (EC2 Spot instances), SNS, and SQS. Connections originate from User to Route 53, resolving to ALB, which forwards traffic to EKS and Spot instances. EKS triggers events to SNS, which routes to SQS, and SQS feeds back to the Spot instance microservices flow.

graph.name: OLX Autos Internal Developer Platform Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture showing how OLX Autos orchestrates dynamic environments using EKS on 100% EC2 Spot Instances with SNS/SQS state handling.

nodes.name: User
nodes.notes: Developer initiating platform environment creation requests.

nodes.name: Route 53
nodes.notes: Handles DNS resolution for the Orion portal.

nodes.name: ALB
nodes.notes: Routes incoming HTTP requests to Kubernetes workloads.

nodes.name: Spot Instances
nodes.notes: Runs workload pods on 100% EC2 Spot instances.

nodes.name: SNS
nodes.notes: Receives events when microservice provisioning jobs are triggered.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Buffers job state messages to allow recovery of interrupted Spot jobs.

edges.notes: User accesses portal via DNS endpoint.
Route 53 resolves DNS to Application Load Balancer.
ALB routes requests to EKS container control plane/pods.
EKS schedules microservice pods onto Spot worker nodes.
EKS job sends completion/status events to SNS.
Replacement jobs poll SQS to recover unfinished microservice deployments.
